title: Plain ETH and Selector Zero
summary: The plain ETH policy tells a real ETH transfer from calldata of four zero bytes. Always Allow cannot.
lesson: Empty calldata and calldata of four zero bytes land on the same rule. Only the plain ETH policy checks that the calldata is really empty, so use it for ETH transfers.

rules.note: Any call to Erin that names no function

steps.label: Send 1 ETH to Dave with four zero bytes
steps.note: Four zero bytes read as selector zero, the same key as no calldata at all. The plain ETH policy looks closer and sees calldata.

steps.label: Send 1 ETH to Erin with four zero bytes
steps.note: Always Allow does not look at calldata. Erin is a person, so nothing runs, but sent to a contract this call would reach the contract's fallback code.

steps.label: Send 0 ETH to Dave
steps.note: A plain transfer has to move some ETH.
